papers.tldr: DynEoMT augments online video segmentation with per-region dynamic/static predictions using only current-frame inputs and propagated queries.

papers.abstract: We present HorizonNav, a video diffusion-based framework for anticipatory robot navigation that transforms a single RGB image and a text prompt into a geometrically aligned representation of plausible surrounding 3D space. Given the initial observation and a textual description of the reconstruction objective, a vision-language model, guided by designed instructions, interprets the scene and constructs structured prompts for a video diffusion model. The resulting video sequence provides plausible future observations of the environment, which are subsequently processed using monocular ORB-SLAM3 for camera pose estimation and Video Depth Anything for dense depth prediction. Our central contribution is a geometry-guided depth alignment stage that combines the estimated camera poses with triangulated visual landmarks to constrain dense depth predictions across multiple views. This alignment improves the geometric consistency of the reconstructed 3D environment, addressing inconsistencies that temporal coherence of the generated video alone cannot resolve. The experimental evaluation of navigation in imagined 3D environment shows that across a 19-scene horizon study, planning-feasible scenes increase from 13/19 at P20 to 15/19 at P81, while successful RRT trials increase from 62/90 to 75/90. In a separate corridor study, 6 of 25 evaluable generated-camera trajectories violate the reconstructed collision constraints; RRT planner recovers feasible alternatives in 5 of those 6 cases. A larger archive contains 58 usable reconstructions from 67 attempted cases, of which 36 support a downstream plan and 22 do not, exposing reconstruction and free-space failure modes rather than hiding them without lidar. Across 15 corridor reconstructions, the mean reconstruction error is approximately 0.30 m at matched structural landmarks.
authors: Hajira Amjad, Valerii Serpiva, Viacheslav Liubimov, Didar Seyidov, Dzmitry Tsetserukou
bullets: Generates plausible future views from one RGB observation plus a textual reconstruction objective.
Uses a vision-language model to guide prompts for video diffusion, then applies ORB-SLAM3 and Video Depth Anything.
Aligns dense depth with camera poses and triangulated landmarks to improve multi-view geometric consistency.
In a 19-scene horizon study, planning-feasible scenes rose from 13/19 to 15/19, and successful RRT trials from 62/90 to 75/90.
The approach remains subject to reconstruction and free-space failures; matched-landmark error was approximately 0.30 m across 15 corridor reconstructions.
papers.selection_reason: Video diffusion world model for anticipatory robot navigation with geometry-guided depth alignment.
papers.title: HorizonNav: Geometry-Guided Video Diffusion for Anticipatory 3D Robot Navigation
papers.tldr: HorizonNav uses text-guided video diffusion and geometry-based depth alignment to imagine and reconstruct navigable 3D surroundings from a single RGB image.

papers.abstract: Classifier-free guidance (CFG) is a standard technique for improving conditional generation in diffusion models, yet its activation schedule is usually selected heuristically. In practice, most existing CFG-based methods rely on a pre-defined activation policy throughout inference, while recent dynamic variants often depend on hand-designed schedules without a principled theoretical explanation of when conditional information is most useful. In order to understand how the informational relevance between conditioning inputs and the score function evolves over the course of generation, we explore when guidance should be activated from an information-theoretic perspective. In this work, we formulate the diffusion trajectory as a time-dependent information bottleneck and show that the effectiveness of conditional information is not uniform throughout sampling, but becomes significantly stronger after a critical stage characterized by a Fisher-information balance condition. Motivated by this insight, we propose a training-free dynamic CFG strategy for inference. Rather than prescribing a fixed schedule in advance, our method constructs a stochastic process from conditional and unconditional score statistics and activates guidance when the estimated guidance gain crosses a prescribed threshold. This yields an adaptive activation rule that aligns condition injection with the underlying generation dynamics, while also recovering interval-based guidance as a limiting special case. Extensive experiments across diverse architectures and tasks, demonstrate that our method is effective, robust, and broadly applicable. Beyond empirical improvements, our framework provides an interpretation of dynamic guidance methods and a principled foundation for inference-time control in conditional diffusion models.
authors: Jiayang Gao, Tianyi Zheng, Jiayang Zou, Fengxiang Yang, Luyao Fan, Lv Tang, Bo Li, Jia Wang
bullets: CFG activation schedules are typically heuristic and fixed or hand-designed.
The diffusion trajectory is modeled as a time-dependent information bottleneck.
Conditional information becomes substantially more useful after a critical stage identified by a Fisher-information balance condition.
A training-free method activates CFG when estimated guidance gain exceeds a threshold, using conditional and unconditional score statistics.
Experiments across architectures and tasks show the approach is effective, robust, and broadly applicable; interval-based guidance emerges as a special case.
papers.selection_reason: Provides a theoretical and practical framework for dynamic Classifier-Free Guidance in diffusion models using an information bottleneck, relevant to video generation and multimodal foundation models.
papers.title: Opening the Black Box of Classifier-Free Guidance via Information Bottleneck
papers.tldr: The paper explains when classifier-free guidance is most informative and uses this insight to adaptively activate guidance during diffusion sampling.

papers.abstract: Video generation supports digital content creation, with applications in virtual avatars, AI-driven filmmaking, interactive game engines, and world models. State-of-the-art systems achieve controllability primarily through image-to-video (I2V) generation, in which an injected anchor image determines the identity, composition, and style of the resulting video. In modern pipelines, this anchor is synthesized by a text-to-image (T2I) generator. This raises a largely overlooked question: Are images obtained directly from the T2I model truly suitable for current video models? Our analysis shows that anchor aesthetic and quality scores are weakly correlated with downstream video quality. The structure-and-texture score is negatively correlated with I2V video quality in both the visual and motion dimensions. Fine-tuning the T2I model on an image reward accordingly yields anchors with visibly denser structural and character detail: they score higher on image metrics, yet lower the video reward on every I2V model we test and change downstream motion unpredictably. We therefore introduce Golden Anchor Learning (GAL), to our knowledge the first framework for learning golden anchors by optimizing a T2I generator with downstream video feedback. GAL evaluates candidate anchors through the videos they induce under a frozen I2V model and converts video rewards into image-level preferences for DPO fine-tuning of the T2I generator. On all four I2V models, GAL raises the VBench average by $2.97\%$--$8.46\%$ over the untuned generator. The rendered clips also score higher under VideoReward-Overall, and their extracted frames under HPSv3 and UniPercept. GAL yields consistent motion gains across all four I2V models, as measured by a $5.62\%$--$38.24\%$ increase in VBench dynamic degree. Although GAL is trained only on HunyuanVideo-1.5 renders, these gains extend to the other three I2V models.
authors: Jinyuan Xu, Shitong Shao, Lichen Bai, Zikai Zhou, Guoxi Huang, Nantheera Anantrasirichai, Zeke Xie
bullets: Image aesthetic and quality scores poorly predict the quality of videos generated from an anchor image.
Fine-tuning the image generator solely on image rewards can worsen video quality and produce unpredictable motion.
GAL evaluates candidate anchors through videos from a frozen I2V model, then uses video-derived preferences for DPO fine-tuning.
Across four I2V models, GAL improves VBench average by 2.97%–8.46% and dynamic degree by 5.62%–38.24%.
Although trained with HunyuanVideo-1.5 renders, GAL’s gains transfer to three other I2V models.
papers.selection_reason: Optimizes text-to-image anchors with downstream video feedback for image-to-video generation, directly relevant to video generation.
papers.title: Golden Anchor for Video Generation
papers.tldr: Golden Anchor Learning improves text-to-image anchor generation for image-to-video systems by optimizing anchors using downstream video feedback.

papers.abstract: Video editing models achieve strong performance in modifying appearance, backgrounds, styles, and motions, empowered by large-scale training data. Beyond general scenarios, professional motions are significant in performance, sports, and martial arts. This paper focuses on professional motion editing, which involves fine-grained motion technique and temporal structure. Given professional motion names but lacking detailed descriptions, existing models often fail to generate professional motions, such as incorrectly lifting the front wheel under a Stoppie instruction. To address this challenge, we introduce MotionCoach, a trained multimodal agent that uses multi-turn tools and performs self-verification, producing a grounded prompt and a reference clip as reliable and sufficient multimodal guidance to inject external professional motion knowledge into video editing models. To supply training data, we build a data pipeline to construct trajectories. We cold-start the agent on MotionCoach-SFT-10k and apply Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on MotionCoach-RL-2k with rewards on the motion guidance prompt, the motion outcome video, and the format. For evaluation, we introduce VPMEBench, comprising 314 professional motion editing tasks with fine-grained references and annotations. Extensive experiments show that MotionCoach improves the overall score from 55.1 to 65.6 on Seedance 2.0 and from 51.2 to 64.5 on MiniMax-H3. Learning to construct multimodal guidance enables precise professional motion editing without retraining video editing models.
authors: Siyi Qian, Hanqing Yang, Weihuang Lin, Zihao Yang, Yichen Lu, Yuanhong Zheng, Sheng Li
bullets: Addresses failures in editing fine-grained professional motions from motion names alone, such as incorrectly performing a Stoppie.
Uses a multimodal agent with multi-turn tools and self-verification to produce a grounded prompt and reference clip.
Trains the agent with supervised fine-tuning and GRPO using rewards for guidance quality, video outcomes, and format.
Introduces VPMEBench, a benchmark of 314 professional motion editing tasks with detailed references and annotations.
Improves evaluation scores from 55.1 to 65.6 on Seedance 2.0 and from 51.2 to 64.5 on MiniMax-H3.
papers.selection_reason: Multimodal guidance construction for professional motion editing in video generation models, relevant to video generation and editing.
papers.title: MotionCoach: Constructing Multimodal Guidance for Video Professional Motion Editing
papers.tldr: MotionCoach generates self-verified text-and-video guidance that helps video editing models perform precise professional motion edits without retraining them.

papers.abstract: Fewer latent tokens promise cheaper diffusion. Yet aggressive latent compression creates a reconstruction-generation dilemma: adding channels improves reconstruction but makes generation harder. We introduce APEX, short for Asynchronous Prefix denoising for EXtreme compression, which pairs a hierarchical latent space with asynchronous denoising over channel groups. Our autoencoder orders channel prefixes from structure to detail, while one shared denoiser generates them at staggered local times without adding tokens. On ImageNet-512, APEX outperforms existing methods at every evaluated channel count under 64x and 128x compression. At matched training and guided sampling compute, it also outperforms a 256-token model at every evaluated budget, with larger gains at lower compute. Code is available at https://daviddinkevich.github.io/APEX.
authors: David Dinkevich, Nisan Chiprut, Yoav HaCohen, Dani Lischinski
bullets: Addresses the reconstruction–generation trade-off in aggressively compressed latent spaces.
Uses an autoencoder with channel prefixes ordered from global structure to fine detail.
A shared denoiser generates channel groups at staggered local times without adding tokens.
On ImageNet-512, it outperforms prior methods across evaluated channel counts at 64× and 128× compression.
It also surpasses a 256-token model at matched compute, with larger gains at lower budgets.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a compression method for diffusion models using asynchronous denoising, improving efficiency in video generation and addressing token management.
papers.title: APEX: Asynchronous Prefix Denoising for Extreme Compression
papers.tldr: APEX enables extreme latent compression by asynchronously denoising hierarchical channel groups, improving image generation quality without increasing token count.

papers.abstract: Modern video-language models are increasingly treated as general-purpose video reasoners, yet it remains unclear whether they robustly capture temporal dynamics in safety-critical settings such as driving. We study this question through controlled ego-motion tasks that require identifying actions from driving videos. Across video-language models, we find that standard prompting, visual prompting, few-shot prompting, and chain-of-thought prompting remain unreliable and highly task- and model-dependent, with persistent class biases, although newer models show substantial task-specific few-shot gains. In contrast, lightweight LoRA finetuning and simple probes trained on intermediate visual features recover strong motion-discriminative performance, indicating that motion-relevant cues are often present inside the models but are not reliably used by the final video-to-language pathway. These results suggest that, in driving, current video-language models remain unreliable temporal reasoners and often behave more like frame-level, bias-driven recognizers than dependable temporal world models.
authors: Shiva Sreeram, Erfan Aasi, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Alaa Maalouf, Daniela Rus
bullets: The study evaluates temporal understanding through controlled ego-motion action-identification tasks in driving videos.
Standard, visual, few-shot, and chain-of-thought prompting are unreliable and strongly dependent on the task and model.
Models exhibit persistent class biases, though newer systems can gain substantially from task-specific few-shot examples.
Lightweight LoRA finetuning and probes on intermediate visual features achieve strong motion discrimination.
Findings suggest final video-to-language pathways underuse temporal cues, causing models to act more like frame-level recognizers than temporal world models.
papers.selection_reason: Evaluation of temporal reasoning in video-language models for driving.
papers.title: Mind the Temporal Gap: Evaluating Video Models for Temporal Understanding in Driving
papers.tldr: Current video-language models often fail to reliably understand temporal dynamics in driving videos, despite containing motion-relevant information that lightweight adaptation can unlock.

papers.abstract: Online reinforcement learning (RL) fine-tunes diffusion models with black-box rewards, but reverse-process methods such as Flow-GRPO are limited in efficiency by poor credit assignment, while forward-process methods such as DiffusionNFT are efficient yet unstable without carefully tuned exponential-moving-average (EMA) off-policy training. We show that NFT-style objectives contain a hidden forward--reverse consistency force that joint positive--negative training cancels only partially, and that EMA stabilizes training through restoration rather than off-policy rollouts. We introduce DiffusionART (Diffusion Reinforcement with Aggregation-First Reward Tilting), which aggregates each prompt's rewards into a shared reward-improving direction for reverse-process states, removing the consistency force by construction, and adds a trust-region-masked second update for drift-adaptive restoration without EMA tuning. It requires no differentiable reward model, remains effective with fewer samples per prompt, and supports pairwise reward models (DiffusionART-Pairwise). Across image and video generation, DiffusionART trains efficiently and stably without per-task tuning. In particular, on HunyuanVideo-13B with equally weighted visual and motion quality rewards, DiffusionART reaches the late-stage mean reward levels of DiffusionNFT and Flow-GRPO-Fast with 12.02 and 11.72 times fewer GPU hours, respectively, while achieving 28.8% and 53.0% higher mean training rewards.
authors: Zhenglin Wan, Jiayu Chen, Zhengfeiyang Zhang, Pengfei Zhou, Wangbo Zhao, Fangyuan Kong, Pengfei Wan, Kun Gai, Yang You
bullets: Addresses inefficient credit assignment in reverse-process RL and instability in forward-process methods.
Aggregates per-prompt rewards into a shared reward-improving direction for reverse-process states, eliminating a conflicting consistency force.
Uses a trust-region-masked second update for drift-adaptive restoration instead of carefully tuned EMA training.
Requires no differentiable reward model, works with fewer samples per prompt, and supports pairwise rewards through DiffusionART-Pairwise.
Across image and video generation, it achieves comparable late-stage rewards with substantially fewer GPU hours and higher mean training rewards on HunyuanVideo-13B.
papers.selection_reason: Reinforcement-learning fine-tuning method for diffusion models, demonstrated on image and video generation.
papers.title: DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models
papers.tldr: DiffusionART is an efficient and stable online-RL method for fine-tuning diffusion models that improves reward optimization while avoiding EMA tuning and costly reverse-process training.

papers.abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) generate discrete data by iteratively unmasking multiple tokens in parallel using a learned mask predictor. Their output carries two errors: parallelization error due to parallel sampling, and estimation error from the mask predictor learned with finite samples. Existing theory treats these errors separately, and the available statistical bounds typically scale with the number $V^L$ of length-$L$ sequences over a vocabulary of size $V$, suffering from the curse of dimensionality. In this work, we establish end-to-end statistical guarantees showing that transformer-based MDMs learn structured distributions with a sample complexity governed by their latent structure. Specifically, we model this structure through mixtures of hidden Markov trees, which capture latent dependencies within components and heterogeneity across components. When the data distribution is well approximated by such a mixture, a transformer-based MDM with parallel unmasking schedules achieves $\varepsilon$-accurate sampling in KL divergence with $\widetilde{O}(LK_{\mathrm{par}}/\varepsilon)$ training samples, where $K_{\mathrm{par}}$ is polynomial in $L$, $V$, the number of hidden states, and the number of mixture components. The transformer network and sampling procedure require no knowledge of the tree topologies or component parameters, thereby adapting to the unknown latent structure automatically. Overall, our results provide theoretical justification for the empirical effectiveness of MDMs on real-world data.
bullets: Addresses both parallelization and finite-sample estimation errors in masked diffusion models.
Models structured data as mixtures of hidden Markov trees, capturing latent dependencies and component heterogeneity.
Proves end-to-end ε-accurate sampling in KL divergence with approximately O(LK_par/ε) training samples.
The polynomial factor K_par depends on sequence length, vocabulary size, hidden states, and mixture components.
The method adapts to unknown tree topologies and component parameters without requiring them as input.
papers.selection_reason: Provides theoretical guarantees for transformer-based Masked Diffusion Models learning structured distributions, bridging video understanding and latent dynamics prediction.
papers.title: Transformer-Based Masked Diffusion Models Provably Learn Distributions with Latent Structure
papers.tldr: Transformer-based masked diffusion models can learn discrete distributions with latent structure using sample complexity that depends on the structure rather than the full sequence space.

papers.abstract: Training-free feature reuse accelerates diffusion transformer inference by replacing full denoising computation at selected steps with cached approximations. Existing methods mainly improve the reconstruction of skipped features, but we find that once a stable first-order reconstructor is used, increasing reconstruction complexity brings limited gains, whereas the placement of exact-computation steps has a much larger effect on fidelity. More importantly, absolute shallow-probe variation is jointly affected by input-trajectory displacement and network response strength, and therefore does not directly reflect cache risk. We address this confounding by normalizing probe-output variation with the corresponding input displacement, yielding a directional gain per unit trajectory movement. Based on this signal, we propose CacheScope, which identifies high-risk reuse steps online and selectively falls back to full denoising computation while leaving the underlying cache reconstructor unchanged. CacheScope requires no additional training, gradients, auxiliary networks, or prompt-specific offline schedule optimization. Across FLUX.1-dev, Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B, and Open-Sora 1.2, CacheScope achieves up to 3.57x acceleration and reduces median LPIPS by up to 70.1% over the strongest probe-based baseline.
authors: Qinhan Lyu, Jusheng Zhang, Zhixing Zhang, Hao Liu, Zijie Liang, Jin Jiang, Keze Wang
bullets: Exact-step placement matters more than increasing the complexity of a stable cache-feature reconstructor.
Raw shallow-probe variation confounds input-trajectory movement with network response strength and can misestimate cache risk.
CacheScope normalizes probe-output variation by input displacement to estimate directional gain per unit movement.
It selectively falls back to full denoising at high-risk steps while keeping the existing cache reconstructor unchanged.
Across three diffusion models, it reduces median LPIPS by up to 70.1% versus the strongest probe-based baseline.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes CacheScope, a method to accelerate diffusion transformer inference by identifying high-risk steps for exact computation, directly relevant to video diffusion acceleration.
papers.title: CacheScope: Exact-Compute Allocation for Training-Free Diffusion Acceleration
papers.tldr: CacheScope accelerates training-free diffusion inference by allocating exact computation to high-risk denoising steps identified through normalized probe variation, achieving up to 3.57× speedup with substantially better fidelity.

papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion models maintain a growing attention key-value (KV) cache, making memory a key bottleneck for long video generation. Recently, clustering-based quantization has emerged as an effective method to compress video KV caches by grouping similar key and value vectors then quantizing residual errors. However, when later frames attend to the compressed history, small reconstruction errors can compound as the video grows. Beyond the within-layer similarity exploited by clustering, we find strong dependencies across cache layers in video models. This motivates Coral-KV - Calibrated Offline, Residual-coded, and Adapted Locally - a KV-cache compression framework that uses cache states in each layer to predict keys and values in subsequent layers, then quantizes the remaining prediction residuals. We construct compact block-diagonal-plus-low-rank (block-DPLR) predictors: block-diagonal components model channel relationships within each attention head, while a global low-rank term models dependencies between heads. Coral-KV exposes a flexible fidelity-memory trade-off: it can reuse its predictors across videos or refit lightweight block-diagonal predictors to the current video for higher fidelity. Across extensive evaluations on both HY-WorldPlay and MAGI-1, our reusable configuration improves PSNR over QVG-4 by 0.32 dB and 4.95 dB, respectively, while using 48% and 37% less cache memory. Against QVG-Pro, our video-adapted configuration improves MAGI-1 PSNR by 3.77 dB while using 33.7% less cache memory. Coral-KV also maintains higher reconstruction fidelity over extended generation and reduces temporal discontinuities while retaining comparable generation latency.
authors: Albert Ge, Akash Haridas, Utkarsh Saxena, Ruijing Yang, Ian Colbert, Frederic Sala, Vikram Appia, Emad Barsoum
bullets: Addresses growing KV-cache memory and error accumulation in long video diffusion generation.
Uses block-diagonal-plus-low-rank predictors to capture within-head channel and across-head dependencies.
Supports reusable predictors for efficiency or lightweight video-specific refitting for higher fidelity.
Improves PSNR while reducing cache memory versus QVG-4 and QVG-Pro across HY-WorldPlay and MAGI-1.
Maintains fidelity over extended generation and reduces temporal discontinuities with comparable latency.
papers.selection_reason: KV-cache compression for autoregressive video diffusion models; directly relevant to memory-efficient inference and video generation.
papers.title: CORAL-KV: Compact Cross-Layer Prediction and Residual Coding for Autoregressive Video KV Caches
papers.tldr: Coral-KV compresses autoregressive video KV caches by predicting later-layer states from earlier layers and quantizing only the residuals, reducing memory while preserving video quality.

papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve remarkable performance in video synthesis, but their iterative denoising process suffers from high inference latency. To address this, caching has emerged as an effective acceleration strategy by capitalizing on inter-step redundancy during denoising. Existing dynamic caching methods typically estimate the error that cache reuse would introduce at each denoising step (step error) to guide cache decisions, whereas our concern is how much quality loss cache reuse would cause in the final generated video (terminal error). We show that step error does not directly correspond to terminal error and that latent information helps capture their relationship, thereby informing cache decisions. Moreover, existing threshold-based methods cannot provide precise speedup control, making it difficult to meet practical requirements for user-specified acceleration targets. To address these limitations, we introduce MORCA, a cache scheduling framework trained through offline-to-online reinforcement learning to make latent-aware reuse/recompute decisions under user-specified acceleration targets. Extensive experiments on different video generation models across multiple target acceleration ratios demonstrate that MORCA achieves better generation fidelity than state-of-the-art caching methods under comparable computational budgets. Code is available at https://github.com/x10ngyx/MORCA.
bullets: Existing caching methods optimize per-step error, which does not reliably reflect final video quality loss.
MORCA learns the relationship between latent information, cache decisions, and terminal generation error.
Its policy makes reuse-versus-recompute decisions under explicit acceleration targets, offering finer speedup control than threshold-based methods.
Experiments across multiple video generation models and acceleration ratios show better fidelity than prior caching methods at comparable computational budgets.
papers.selection_reason: RL-based cache reuse to accelerate video diffusion; fits efficient inference and video diffusion.
papers.title: MORCA: Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Cache Reuse in Video Diffusion Acceleration
papers.tldr: MORCA uses latent-aware offline-to-online reinforcement learning to adaptively schedule cache reuse in video diffusion, improving fidelity while meeting user-specified acceleration targets.

papers.abstract: Video tokenizers have emerged as a cornerstone of modern video modeling, underpinning progress in compression, reconstruction and generation by mapping high-dimensional visual signals into compact latent spaces. However, despite this progress, current tokenization paradigms largely remain within the 2D visual domain, treating videos as image sequences rather than observations of an underlying dynamic 3D world. Consequently, the learned tokens inherit this observation-centric bias, limiting their capacity to compactly represent real-world 4D scenes. To mitigate this issue, we propose VideoTok4D, a novel 4D-aware video tokenizer for compact world representation. Specifically, our approach comprises three key designs: 1) a spatiotemporal disentanglement strategy that factorizes videos into static and dynamic tokens for holistic world modeling; 2) a track-aware dynamic attention mechanism that aggregates trajectory-aligned cues to promote cross-view motion consistency; and 3) Co4DGen, a diffusion prior learned over the resulting VideoTok4D token space for efficient 4D scene generation. Extensive experiments have demonstrated that our proposed method achieves state-of-the-art performance while requiring up to 4 orders of magnitude less storage than dense 4D representations. Moreover, the compact token space substantially shortens diffusion sequences, enabling efficient generation.
bullets: Addresses the limitation of 2D, image-sequence-based video tokenizers for representing dynamic 3D worlds.
Disentangles videos into static and dynamic tokens for holistic world modeling.
Uses track-aware dynamic attention to aggregate trajectory-aligned cues and improve cross-view motion consistency.
Introduces Co4DGen, a diffusion prior over the token space for efficient 4D scene generation.
Reports state-of-the-art performance with up to 4 orders of magnitude less storage than dense 4D representations, while shortening diffusion sequences.
papers.selection_reason: 4D-aware video tokenizer for compact world representation and diffusion-based 4D generation.
papers.title: VideoTok4D: A 4D-Aware Video Tokenizer for Compact World Representation
papers.tldr: VideoTok4D builds a compact 4D-aware video tokenization framework that separates static and dynamic content, captures trajectory-consistent motion, and enables efficient 4D scene generation.

papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models learn mostly from paired image-text data or annotated video, and raw web video is rarely used to further train an existing language model. We study whether raw video, with no captions and no text loss, can serve as mid-training data for a pretrained language model. Frames are encoded into continuous visual tokens, and the language model learns to predict the next visual token. We mid-train Qwen3-1.7B on raw clips from YT-Temporal-1B and then apply the same image-text instruction tuning to it and to the model without mid-training, so that the two differ only in mid-training. The mid-trained model scores 2.9 points higher on average across four video benchmarks and 5.1 points higher across ten image benchmarks, spanning perception, document, and chart tasks. Text performance is preserved even though mid-training includes no text, with an average of 48.9 across 14 text benchmarks compared with 48.0 for the model without mid-training. Analyses across training show that the image and video gains emerge within 30% of training and plateau thereafter, varying by less than 0.5 points. Predicting captions fails to outperform next-visual-token prediction, demonstrating that video mid-training can remain purely self-supervised without the computational overhead or labeling noise of automated captioning.
authors: Jaedong Hwang, Xiaoqian Shen, Ernie Chang, Changsheng Zhao, Chong Zhou, Saksham Suri, Qi Qian, Zechun Liu, Lemeng Wu, Qinsi Wang, Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi, Wei Wen
bullets: Raw, uncaptained web video can be used to mid-train a pretrained language model.
The method encodes frames as continuous visual tokens and trains the model to predict the next visual token.
After identical image-text instruction tuning, mid-training yields +2.9 average points on four video benchmarks and +5.1 on ten image benchmarks.
Text performance is preserved: 48.9 average across 14 text benchmarks versus 48.0 without mid-training.
Gains appear early and plateau; caption prediction does not outperform next-visual-token prediction.
papers.selection_reason: Self-supervised raw-video mid-training of MLLMs via next visual token prediction improves video and image understanding.
papers.title: Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video
papers.tldr: Mid-training a language model on raw video by predicting visual tokens improves downstream video and image understanding while preserving text performance, without captions or text supervision.

papers.abstract: Recent 3D world models generate photorealistic, explorable scenes that remain frozen in time. OuroWorld is a mask-free framework that turns any static 3D Gaussian Splatting scene into a 3D cinemagraph: a dynamic scene with vivid, diverse motion looping seamlessly from any viewpoint. A vision-language model infers plausible dynamics and guides a video model to synthesize a reference video, which we lift and complete into multi-view videos. To learn from this imperfect supervision, we propose Inconsistency-Robust Periodic 4DGS: a Fourier-series deformation field guarantees looping by construction, while a Grounded Drift Field anchored at the reference view absorbs cross-view inconsistency. Unlike prior Eulerian methods limited to fluid-like motion, we capture general deformation, object motion, and illumination change. We introduce a ground-truth-free evaluation covering vividness, naturalness, loop seam coherence, and scene quality. On 39 reconstructed and generated scenes, OuroWorld outperforms all baselines and wins 70.8%-99.0% of user-study comparisons. Project page: https://ouroworld.userwei.com
authors: You-Zhe Xie, Ting-Wei Chou, Yu-Hsuan Li, Kaipeng Zhang, Zhixiang Wang, Yu-Lun Liu
bullets: Addresses the limitation that photorealistic 3D world models are typically static.
Uses a vision-language model and video model to infer and synthesize plausible motion, then lifts it into multi-view videos.
Introduces Inconsistency-Robust Periodic 4DGS, combining Fourier deformation fields for guaranteed loops with a reference-anchored drift field for cross-view inconsistencies.
Supports object deformation, object motion, and illumination changes beyond fluid-like motion.
Evaluated on 39 scenes with a ground-truth-free metric suite; the abstract reports outperforming all baselines and winning 70.8%–99.0% of user-study comparisons.
papers.selection_reason: Turns static 3D scenes into looping dynamic 3D cinemagraphs; fits 3D scene generation and video synthesis.
papers.title: OuroWorld: Bringing Any 3D World Alive as Diverse, Endlessly Looping 3D Cinemagraphs
papers.tldr: OuroWorld transforms static 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes into viewpoint-consistent, diverse, seamlessly looping 3D cinemagraphs with general scene motion and lighting changes.

papers.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are rapidly evolving toward continuous audio--visual reasoning, creating an urgent need for evaluations that expose their capability limits. Audio--visual captioning is an ideal diagnostic task, yet current benchmarks face a coupled trade-off: whole-caption scores provide coverage without localization, local probes provide localization without coverage, and unconstrained LLM judges introduce instability. We introduce OmniCapBench (Omni-Video Caption Benchmark), a benchmark that reframes audio--visual caption evaluation as a deep-structured diagnostic framework. OmniCapBench shifts the prediction target from free-form text to sets of atomic, verifiable evaluation units across three tracks: entity references, visual shots, and audio events, enabling reliable scoring with deterministic constraint checks and localized LLM-based semantic comparisons. With 786 densely annotated videos, OmniCapBench effectively distinguishes MLLM perception errors, including temporal grounding failures, identity drift, cross-modal misalignment, and hallucinated descriptions. Evaluating frontier MLLMs reveals strong local perception but weak long-horizon audio--visual reasoning, particularly in identity drift and cross-modal misalignment, providing a fine-grained roadmap for omnimodal development.
authors: Zhongyu Yang, Jiale Tao, Ruitao Chen, Zuhao Yang, Yingfang Yuan, Xueliang Zhao, Auden, Kai Wang, Shuai Shao, Biao Wang, Steve Yves, Qinglin Lu
bullets: Addresses the trade-off between broad whole-caption coverage, localized evaluation, and unstable unconstrained LLM judging.
Decomposes captions into three tracks: entity references, visual shots, and audio events.
Combines deterministic constraint checks with localized LLM-based semantic comparisons for reliable scoring.
Uses 786 densely annotated videos to identify temporal grounding failures, identity drift, cross-modal misalignment, and hallucinations.
Finds that frontier MLLMs show strong local perception but weaker long-horizon audio-visual reasoning, especially for identity drift and cross-modal alignment.
papers.selection_reason: Fine-grained audio-visual captioning benchmark for MLLMs; fits video understanding and multimodal LLM evaluation.
papers.title: OmniCapBench: A Deep-Structured Evaluation Framework for Fine-Grained Audio-Visual Captioning
papers.tldr: OmniCapBench evaluates audio-visual captioning through atomic, verifiable units to diagnose fine-grained MLLM perception and reasoning failures.

papers.abstract: On a film set, the camera move is committed during a take. Generative video reshooting lets filmmakers change it afterward, but may require hallucinating unrecorded content, a gap sometimes discovered only after leaving the set. We present Hybrid Cinematography, a workflow that bridges physical capture and generative reshooting to manage hallucination risk while filmmakers can still act on it. Using an editable 3D shot plan and a proxy of the take, our previsualization evaluates hallucination risk in real time. Seeing where the take lacks support, filmmakers can iteratively adjust the plan, explore moves that balance capture and generation, shoot guided pickups, or knowingly accept hallucination. We demonstrate the workflow through a mobile augmented reality application for on-set planning, capture, and review, and an offline pipeline for existing video. A study with experienced filmmakers reveals how previsualizing risk informs camera decisions and exposes tensions between creative intent and generative hallucination.
authors: Nhan (Nathan), Tran, Neal Wadhwa, Abe Davis, Stefan Stojanov
bullets: Addresses the gap between committed physical camera captures and post hoc generative reshooting.
Uses an editable 3D shot plan and take proxy to evaluate hallucination risk during previsualization.
Supports iterative planning, guided pickups, capture–generation trade-offs, and intentional acceptance of hallucination.
Demonstrated through a mobile augmented-reality tool for on-set planning and an offline pipeline for existing video.
A study with experienced filmmakers shows that risk visualization informs camera decisions while revealing tensions with creative intent.
papers.selection_reason: Develops a workflow for managing hallucination risk in generative video reshooting, combining physical capture with generative models, relevant to video generation techniques.
papers.title: Hybrid Cinematography: Previsualizing and Managing Hallucination Risk in Generative Video Reshooting
papers.tldr: Hybrid Cinematography helps filmmakers preview and manage the risk of hallucinated content when changing camera moves in generative video reshooting.

papers.abstract: Generating an egocentric video from a single exocentric recording is a challenging case of novel view synthesis, as the two cameras share little overlap and much of the target view is unobserved. Current state-of-the-art methods reconstruct the scene explicitly by estimating depth, lifting the video into a point cloud, and re-rendering it from the egocentric camera to condition a video diffusion model. This deterministic mapping assigns each pixel to a single reprojected location, which preserves texture but translates depth errors into misplaced content. We ask what a video diffusion model should receive as its condition and propose a lifting-free answer: a learned view synthesizer, an LVSM-style transformer fine-tuned to render the egocentric view directly without depth, point clouds, or reprojection, resolving cross-view correspondence internally. In contrast, its probabilistic mapping averages each region over candidate source locations according to a learned correspondence distribution, preserving structure while fine texture is averaged away. We argue that this trade-off suits a diffusion generator, whose denoising training excels at restoring detail, so an effective condition should prioritize structural alignment over sharpness. This distribution's concentration also yields a per-region confidence, used both to mask low-confidence regions and to guide the generator toward high-confidence areas during early layout-forming denoising steps. Our approach consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art explicit pipeline and generalizes to other datasets without retraining. The synthesizer thus supplies view structure, and the diffusion model its detail.
authors: Suhwan Cho, Yonwoo Choi, Soongjin Kim, Jicheol Park, Taegyu Lim
bullets: Addresses exocentric-to-egocentric synthesis when the target view has little camera overlap and substantial unobserved content.
Uses an LVSM-style transformer to render the target view directly, avoiding depth estimation, point clouds, and reprojection.
Models cross-view correspondence probabilistically, favoring structural alignment over potentially misplaced sharp details.
Uses correspondence confidence to mask uncertain regions and guide early diffusion denoising.
Outperforms the prior explicit pipeline and transfers to other datasets without retraining, according to the abstract.
papers.selection_reason: Egocentric video generation via diffusion conditioned on learned view synthesis; fits video diffusion and novel view synthesis.
papers.title: LEGO: A Lifting-Free Approach for Exocentric-to-Egocentric Video Generation
papers.tldr: LEGO replaces depth-based view lifting with a learned view synthesizer that provides structurally aligned egocentric conditions for diffusion-based video generation.

papers.abstract: Streaming Video Large Language Models (VLMs) enable continuous video understanding, yet existing benchmarks focus on low-dynamic scenarios. Under bounded context budgets, models must balance temporal history, spatial resolution, and temporal granularity; sparse sampling at 1--2 FPS misses fast events. We introduce FastBench to evaluate high-dynamic perception in real-world video streams. Its trajectory-grounded pipeline combines QA generation from high-FPS clips, filtering of questions answerable at 2 FPS, answer verification using SAM3 and CoTracker3 trajectories, and three rounds of human inspection. FastBench contains 306 QA pairs across eight domains, six capabilities, and forward, instant, and backward temporal scopes, with human-annotated evidence intervals. We also present ProactiveFrame, a training-free baseline that adjusts incoming frame rates through text tokens. A dual-tier sliding window retains recent high-FPS observations while downsampling older ones into sparse history. Experiments reveal substantial limitations: the strongest model, Gemini-3.5-Flash, scores only 50.7%. Denser sampling improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 32.9% at 2 FPS to 44.6% at 24 FPS, but gains saturate as history is compressed. ProactiveFrame outperforms sparse uniform sampling by 5.4 and 1.5 percentage points, yet remains well below oracle-guided focusing, showing that current VLMs struggle to determine from the stream alone when finer temporal perception is needed. FastBench provides a testbed for high-dynamic streaming video understanding. Code and data: https://github.com/Ashone3/FastBench.
authors: Yuxuan Hu, Weikang Shi, Yang Bo, Xudong Lu, Xintong Guo, Shuhan Li, Yuyang He, Huankang Guan, Peiwen Sun, Yunqiao Yang, Wenbo Li, Rui Liu, Hongsheng Li
bullets: Introduces a benchmark for high-dynamic real-world video understanding across eight domains, six capabilities, and multiple temporal scopes.
Builds 306 QA pairs from high-FPS clips with trajectory-based verification, human inspection, and annotated evidence intervals.
ProactiveFrame adaptively adjusts frame rates using text tokens and a dual-tier sliding window.
The strongest evaluated model reaches only 50.7%; Qwen3-VL-8B improves from 32.9% at 2 FPS to 44.6% at 24 FPS.
Adaptive sampling beats sparse uniform sampling but remains far below oracle-guided focusing, revealing difficulty in knowing when finer temporal perception is needed.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmark for high-dynamic streaming video understanding with VLMs; fits video understanding and multimodal LLM evaluation.
papers.title: FastBench: Can Streaming VLMs Perceive High-Dynamic Real-World Streams?
papers.tldr: FastBench shows that current streaming VLMs struggle to perceive fast events, even with denser frame sampling or adaptive streaming strategies.

papers.abstract: Single-image, multi-image, and video deep research require different visual operations but share a workflow of visual grounding, external retrieval, and fact composition. A key challenge is to preserve the dependencies linking localized visual anchors, entity relations, source-supported facts, and answer-producing operations. We introduce OneSearch-VL, a unified agent centered on the Visually Grounded Evidence Graph (VGEG), which encodes these dependencies as a shared task-level reference for data construction, process supervision, and operation-level evaluation. Our VGEG-based data engine constructs and verifies multi-image and video questions and filters expert trajectories. Using these data, we assemble OneSearch-VL-SFT-110K and OneSearch-VL-RL-10K for SFT and RL, respectively. We further derive the Evidence-aware Visual-Grounded Rubric reward (EVGR) from VGEG annotations to supervise evidence traceability and visual grounding during RL. For fine-grained evaluation, we construct OneSearch-MI-Bench and OneSearch-Video-Bench, organizing questions by the research operations encoded in their VGEGs. Experiments show that OneSearch-VL-8B improves over Qwen3-VL-8B with tool access by 20.2 and 17.6 percentage points on the two new benchmarks, respectively, while also achieving substantial gains across 7 image benchmarks and VideoDR. Project repository: https://github.com/appletea233/OneSearch-VL
authors: Hongyu Li, Manyuan Zhang, Kaituo Feng, Shu Chen, Dian Zheng, Hao Li, Hao Yu, Zhangquan Chen, Zoey Guo, Ray Zhang, Shaofei Huang, Tianrui Hui, Linjiang Huang, Si Liu
bullets: Addresses the challenge of preserving links among visual regions, entities, retrieved evidence, and answer-generating operations.
Introduces the Visually Grounded Evidence Graph (VGEG) as a shared representation for data construction, process supervision, and operation-level evaluation.
Provides SFT/RL training resources and the evidence-aware EVGR reward for improving visual grounding and evidence traceability.
Builds fine-grained multi-image and video benchmarks organized by research operations.
The 8B model outperforms Qwen3-VL-8B with tool access by 20.2 and 17.6 percentage points on the two new benchmarks, with additional gains on seven image benchmarks and VideoDR.
papers.selection_reason: Unified multimodal research agent with visual grounding and video/image deep research; fits VLM-based reasoning and video understanding.
papers.title: OneSearch-VL: Unified Multimodal Deep Research Agent for Image and Video
papers.tldr: OneSearch-VL unifies image and video deep research through a visually grounded evidence graph that guides data, training, rewards, and evaluation.

papers.abstract: Faithful visual world simulation requires generated videos to maintain 4D world consistency, encompassing both static and dynamic consistency. Static consistency requires coherent 3D structure in static environments across viewpoints, while dynamic consistency requires plausible subject motion and consistent appearance over time. Geometry-aware post-training offers a promising way to improve world consistency. However, existing methods often rely on a static-scene assumption. Even those that accommodate dynamic scenes struggle to provide reliable static-consistency feedback, while dynamic consistency is often overlooked or inadequately assessed. To address these limitations, we introduce WorldAlign, a decoupled 4D reward framework that semantically separates static regions and dynamic subjects and provides feedback by aligning each with a world prior suited to its assumptions. For static regions, WorldAlign aligns static geometry with a geometric world prior through semantically guided masked reprojection, enabling more reliable static-consistency evaluation; an auxiliary camera-motion reward discourages nearly static solutions. For dynamic subjects, WorldAlign uses a strong vision-language model (VLM) as a dynamic world prior and constructs a VLM-as-a-judge reward based on sample-specific checklists that assess dynamicity, physical plausibility, shape, and texture consistency. This decoupled design enables more effective online post-training without requiring human preference annotations. Across two pretrained image-to-video generators, Wan2.1 and Wan2.2, WorldAlign jointly improves static and dynamic consistency over existing methods without suppressing overall or subject motion. These results support decoupled world-prior alignment for more faithful visual world simulation. Project page: https://worldalign.github.io/.
authors: Jing He, Kaixin Ding, Xingye Tian, Guibao Shen, Wenhang Ge, Xin Tao, Pengfei Wan, Ying-Cong Chen
bullets: Addresses the challenge of jointly maintaining static scene structure and plausible, consistent motion in generated videos.
Separates static regions from dynamic subjects and aligns each with a suitable world prior.
Uses masked geometric reprojection plus a camera-motion reward for static consistency.
Uses VLM-generated, sample-specific checklist judgments for dynamicity, physical plausibility, shape, and texture consistency.
Improves both static and dynamic consistency across Wan2.1 and Wan2.2 without suppressing overall or subject motion, and requires no human preference annotations.
papers.selection_reason: Reward framework for world-consistent video generation; relevant to video diffusion and world-consistent simulation.
papers.title: WorldAlign: Decoupled 4D Reward for World-Consistent Video Generation
papers.tldr: WorldAlign improves video world consistency by separately rewarding static 3D geometry and dynamic subject behavior during post-training.

papers.abstract: Generative diffusion models are well-suited for probabilistic precipitation nowcasting, but existing approaches often rely on separately trained compression or deterministic forecasting components and remain costly at inference due to iterative denoising. We introduce Just Weather Scoring (JWS), a single-stage, end-to-end diffusion model which addresses both issues by forecasting directly in radar space and enabling few-step generation. Radar-space modeling greatly simplifies training and inference and eliminates uncertainty arising from lossy compression. JWS combines Masked Asynchronous Diffusion, a timestep-sampling scheme that preserves clean context while adapting diffusion training to high-dimensional spatio-temporal data, with a simple scoring-rule objective that aligns training with probabilistic forecasting and unlocks few-step generation. On the SEVIR and MeteoNet benchmarks, JWS achieves state-of-the-art probabilistic forecasting performance at reduced training and inference cost. Even our smallest model remains competitive using substantially fewer parameters and more than 17x faster inference.
authors: Jannik Wiese, Johannes Schusterbauer, Tommaso Martorella, Bj\"orn Ommer
bullets: Avoids separately trained compression and deterministic forecasting components by modeling directly in radar space.
Uses Masked Asynchronous Diffusion to preserve clean context while training on high-dimensional spatio-temporal data.
Applies a scoring-rule objective designed for probabilistic forecasting and few-step generation.
Achieves state-of-the-art probabilistic forecasting on SEVIR and MeteoNet at lower training and inference cost.
The smallest model remains competitive with over 17× faster inference and substantially fewer parameters.
papers.selection_reason: Addresses probabilistic precipitation nowcasting using a single-stage distributional diffusion model (JWS) that operates in radar space, offering efficient few-step generation.
papers.title: Just Weather Scoring: Efficient End-to-end Nowcasting with Distributional Diffusion
papers.tldr: JWS is an end-to-end radar-space diffusion model that enables accurate probabilistic precipitation nowcasting with few-step, substantially faster inference.

papers.abstract: To stream long videos while maintaining visual quality and temporal consistency, Self Forcing mitigates exposure bias through self-rollout training on self-generated histories with key-value (KV) caching. To keep memory manageable, it detaches historical caches, preserving forward dependencies between chunks but severing the backward gradient paths. We introduce Connected Self Forcing, a training framework that reconnects gradient paths across autoregressive chunks, allowing feedback from later predictions to guide how earlier context is generated. These connections go beyond historical KV-writing: gradients pass through generated latents into the computations that produced them, linking the generation of earlier context to its use in later predictions. To make this connected training memory-efficient, we develop shortcut gradient replay, which recovers cross-chunk gradients without retaining the full rollout computation graph. Integrated with distribution matching distillation, Connected Self Forcing trains historical chunks according to both their direct supervision and their contribution to subsequent generation. Experiments on autoregressive video generation show improvements in long-horizon visual quality and temporal consistency, without changing the inference procedure.
authors: Dongbin Zhang, Chaoda Zheng, Kangjie Chen, Xiangyu Li, Shijia Chen, Jinhao Deng, Yuqi Zhang, Guangfeng Jiang, Hongbin Lin, Choo Sin Wai, Minqi Wang, Puyi Wang, Jingye Zhang, Yu Zhang, Xianming Liu, Boyang Wang
bullets: Addresses exposure bias and weak long-range learning caused by detached historical KV caches in Self Forcing.
Reconnects gradient paths across autoregressive chunks, including through generated latents and the computations that produced them.
Introduces shortcut gradient replay to recover cross-chunk gradients without storing the full rollout graph.
Combines connected training with distribution matching distillation, supervising chunks based on both direct accuracy and downstream impact.
Experiments report improved long-horizon visual quality and temporal consistency without modifying inference.
papers.selection_reason: Training framework for autoregressive video generation with cross-chunk gradient connections, directly relevant to autoregressive video models.
papers.title: Connected Self Forcing: Beyond Local Learning in Video Autoregression
papers.tldr: Connected Self Forcing improves long-video autoregressive generation by training earlier context using gradient feedback from later predictions, while keeping inference unchanged.

papers.abstract: Building a capable video editor remains significantly harder than a video generator: editing requires (source, instruction, edited) triplets that are prohibitively expensive to annotate and difficult to synthesize at scale, whereas image editing has already reached maturity with millions of such pairs readily available. In this work, we introduce VINCIE-NExT, a unified framework that transfers editing capability from images to videos through in-context visual demonstrations, alleviating the need for large-scale paired video editing data. VINCIE-NExT decomposes video editing into a structured chain of composable sub-tasks (Video -> Image -> Image -> Video), routing editing intent through the image domain and enabling scalable joint training from heterogeneous image and video corpora under a unified diffusion objective. An image editing pair, synthesized by the model or supplied by the user, is prepended as an in-context visual demonstration that serves as a spatial appearance blueprint for every output frame. To ground appearance edits across the interleaved context, we introduce a novel position encoding that links image demonstrations and video frames in a shared spatial coordinate system, enabling pixel-faithful propagation of appearance changes to every output frame. Chain-of-Editing further provides principled test-time scaling: by executing the sub-task chain as progressive diffusion stages, editing quality can be improved by investing additional compute without retraining. Comprehensive experiments on OpenVE-Bench demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance across diverse editing categories, with ablations confirming the effectiveness of each component.
authors: Leigang Qu, Feng Cheng, Ziyan Yang, Bangbang Yang, Zhaoyang Huang, Wei Chow, Yicong Li, Wenjie Wang, Tat-Seng Chua, Yan Zeng
bullets: Addresses the scarcity and cost of paired video-editing data.
Decomposes video editing into composable sub-tasks and trains jointly on heterogeneous image and video corpora with a unified diffusion objective.
Uses an image-editing pair as a visual demonstration to provide a spatial appearance blueprint for all output frames.
Introduces shared spatial-coordinate positional encoding to propagate appearance edits consistently across frames.
Chain-of-Editing enables test-time quality scaling through progressive diffusion stages; experiments on OpenVE-Bench report state-of-the-art performance across editing categories.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes VINCIE-NExT, a framework for video editing that leverages in-context modeling and image editing capabilities to generate high-quality video edits, addressing the data scarcity of video editing pairs.
papers.title: VINCIE-NExT: Unlocking Video Editing from Images via In-Context Modeling
papers.tldr: VINCIE-NExT enables video editing from mature image-editing data by routing edits through image-based in-context demonstrations and a composable video–image–image–video pipeline.

papers.abstract: Flow matching has emerged as a scalable paradigm for training high-quality generative models, but sampling from the learned probability flow requires many network evaluations. Distillation can reduce this cost to one or a few evaluations; however, one-step generation often sacrifices quality, making few-step generation the practical operating regime. Existing few-step methods perform their iterative computation along the probability flow and therefore require a fixed, manually chosen timestep discretization. This discretization is often chosen heuristically and is expensive to tune; it may also be restrictive when refinement difficulty differs across samples or spatial locations. We introduce data-space iteration, a few-step generation framework that removes flow discretization altogether. Starting from noise, a shared generator directly refines its prediction in data space, with every iteration trained to produce the best sample permitted by its capacity. Our formulation integrates with distribution matching distillation (DMD) with minimal changes, enabling a controlled comparison between iteration methods under matched training settings. On class-conditional ImageNet 256x256, data-space iteration outperforms standard discretization baselines and matches or improves upon variants selected through schedule search, without requiring schedule-specific training. These results show that data-space iteration provides a simple and effective alternative to discretized flow-space iteration for fast generation.
authors: Shanchuan Lin, Yansong Peng, Fu-Yun Wang, Haoqi Fan
bullets: Flow-matching samplers typically require many network evaluations, while one-step distillation can reduce quality.
Existing few-step methods rely on fixed timestep discretizations that are heuristic, costly to tune, and inflexible across samples or regions.
The proposed method repeatedly refines samples directly in data space using a shared generator.
It integrates with distribution matching distillation with minimal changes, enabling matched comparisons.
On class-conditional ImageNet 256×256, it outperforms standard discretization baselines and matches or improves schedule-searched variants without schedule-specific training.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces 'data-space iteration' for few-step generation in diffusion models, removing the need for flow discretization and improving efficiency without schedule-specific training.
papers.title: Few-Step Generation via Data-Space Iteration
papers.tldr: Data-space iteration enables high-quality few-step generation without manually designed or tuned flow-time schedules.

papers.abstract: Continuing the Perception Test challenge series, we organised the fourth edition as a workshop at the European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2026 in Malm\"o, Sweden. This edition focused on spatial intelligence and featured four different tracks: unified multiple-choice videoQA and grounded videoQA from the original Perception Test benchmark, alongside two new tracks based on city-scale walking-tour videos (KilometerAudio and KilometerVision). In this report, we describe the new benchmarks used for the city-scale tracks and summarise the winning solutions across all tracks, including a generalist model that competed across all tracks with satisfactory performance. The winning solutions in the newly added city-scale tracks demonstrated that complex spatial and multimodal reasoning can be solved by expensive agentic pipelines, but remains difficult for multimodal models used standalone.
authors: Fedor Kitashov, Jo\~ao Carreira, Shiry Ginosar, Dima Damen, Andrew Zisserman, Viorica P\u{a}tr\u{a}ucean
bullets: ECCV 2026 challenge focused on spatial intelligence across four tracks.
Retained unified multiple-choice and grounded videoQA tracks from the original benchmark.
Introduced KilometerAudio and KilometerVision tracks using city-scale walking-tour videos.
Summarizes winning solutions, including a generalist model participating across all tracks.
City-scale results suggest agentic pipelines outperform standalone multimodal approaches in handling complex spatial reasoning, without reporting specific metrics.
papers.selection_reason: Challenge summary focused on spatial intelligence and city-scale audio-visual reasoning, relevant to video understanding and spatial multimodal reasoning.
papers.title: Perception Test 2026: Challenge Summary and Extension to City-scale Audio-Visual Reasoning
papers.tldr: The fourth Perception Test challenge expands video reasoning to city-scale audio-visual tasks, showing that spatial multimodal reasoning remains difficult for standalone models but can be tackled with costly agentic pipelines.

papers.abstract: Data video is a media form that integrates data visualization with video narrative, widely adopted in news reporting and business analysis. Compared with general video understanding, data video understanding places greater emphasis on accurately reading data from animated charts, integrating evidence across charts and time, and understanding how narrative organization and visual design communicate information. Yet existing benchmarks target either general videos or static charts, and data video understanding has not been systematically evaluated. We present DataVista, the first benchmark for data video understanding, containing 961 real-world data videos and 6,775 evaluation questions organized under a three-level progressive capability framework (data perception, temporal reasoning, narrative understanding) with 10 fine-grained question types across five topic domains. Systematic evaluation of 19 mainstream MLLMs shows that the best-performing model, Gemini-3.1-Pro, achieves 70.0% overall accuracy, still far below human expert performance, with models performing worst on Causal Reasoning and Narrative Structure. Increasing frame counts and adding subtitles mainly benefit data perception and temporal reasoning, with limited gains in narrative understanding. Further analysis of model responses identifies typical failure modes in chart reading, evidence judgment, and instruction understanding. The benchmark is available at https://github.com/HKUSTDial/DataVista.
authors: Yupeng Xie, Zhenyang Wang, Jiayi Zhu, Yinghao Tang, Zhouan Shen, Yiyu Chen, Yuyu Luo
bullets: Covers 961 real-world data videos and 6,775 questions across 10 question types, five domains, and three capability levels.
Evaluates 19 mainstream multimodal LLMs; the best reported model reaches 70.0% overall accuracy, below expert performance.
Models struggle most with causal reasoning and narrative structure, beyond basic chart reading and temporal reasoning.
More frames and subtitles mainly improve data perception and temporal reasoning, with limited benefit for narrative understanding.
Analysis reveals failures in chart interpretation, evidence judgment, and instruction understanding.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmark for data video understanding evaluates MLLM temporal and video-language reasoning.
papers.title: DataVista: Diagnosing Multimodal LLMs on Data Video Understanding
papers.tldr: DataVista introduces the first benchmark for evaluating multimodal LLMs on understanding animated data visualizations, temporal evidence, and narrative structure in data videos.

papers.abstract: Finding the right video often requires distinguishing similar scenes in which different events occur. Joint matching improves retrieval, but processing rich video representations for each query is costly. VEDJE compresses features within sampled frames while keeping their representations separate in a reusable cache. Feature-change prediction supplies an auxiliary training signal that improves retrieval from the compressed cache without adding work at query time. On MSR-VTT, MSVD, DiDeMo, and ActivityNet, VEDJE improves R@1 over matched first-stage retrievers in both retrieval directions. On MSR-VTT, it reaches 59.8 text-to-video R@1 with a fine-tuned VideoCLIP-XL first stage. In the VideoPrism configuration, shrinking the per-video cache fourfold to 12 KiB preserves text-to-video recall within 0.2 points. These results show that accurate video search can operate on compact evidence, encoded once and reused as new queries arrive.
authors: Shahaf Wagner, Gabriele Serussi, Dan Ben Ami, Tomer Galanti, Chaim Baskin
bullets: Targets the cost of processing rich video representations for every query, especially when similar scenes contain different events.
Compresses features within sampled frames while keeping representations separate in a reusable per-video cache.
Uses feature-change prediction as an auxiliary training signal to improve retrieval from compressed features without added query-time work.
Improves R@1 over matched first-stage retrievers in both directions across MSR-VTT, MSVD, DiDeMo, and ActivityNet.
On MSR-VTT, achieves 59.8 text-to-video R@1 with a fine-tuned VideoCLIP-XL first stage; a fourfold smaller VideoPrism cache retains recall within 0.2 points.
papers.selection_reason: Scalable video-text retrieval with compressed reusable video features; relevant to video-language understanding and efficient retrieval.
papers.title: VEDJE: Video-Efficient Discriminative Joint Encoder for Scalable Video-Text Retrieval
papers.tldr: VEDJE enables accurate video-text retrieval by compressing cached video features while preserving discriminative event information and avoiding extra query-time computation.

papers.abstract: Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization (OV-AVEL) labels each video segment with an event class, including classes that were never seen during training. The dominant pipeline uses a frozen multimodal foundation model (e.g. ImageBind) to embed the visual frame, the audio mel-spectrogram, and each candidate class name into a shared space, then computes two cosine similarities for each segment against each class: visual-text and audio-text. Existing methods then collapse this pair into a single scalar score with a fixed rule (geometric mean, weighted average) before taking the argmax. Instead, we compute complex-valued similarities and learn their fusion using a complex-valued neural network (CVNN). Each modality's standard representation becomes the real part of our pipeline, and a paired companion stream supplies the imaginary part. We use imaginary part of iHSV for visual modality and CycleGAN-translated phase spectrogram for audio modality as these companion streams. This results in two complex similarities, which are then fused. While the vision and audio encoders remain frozen, only the temporal-attention blocks and the fusion CVNN are trained. The four-stream complex architecture sets a new state of the art on both OV-AVEL benchmarks. On the open (unseen-class) split of OV-AVEBench we reach 66.5/59.1/54.1% Acc/Seg-F1/Event-F1 (+1.6/+4.1/+6.6 over the previously reported fine-tuned baseline), with consistent gains for seen classes as well. We also modify AVE dataset for this task and observe that our architecture reaches 60.7/51.9/50.4% Acc/Seg-F1/Event-F1, achieving state-of-the-art OV-AVEL results on it as well. We also propose a two-stream alternative, which also sees great improvements over the baseline.
authors: Anirudh Praveen, Koteswar Rao Jerripothula, Pratik Joshi, Aveen Dayal, Neela Sawant
bullets: Targets event localization for classes unseen during training.
Uses frozen multimodal encoders, with companion visual and audio streams providing imaginary components.
Trains temporal-attention blocks and a complex-valued neural network to fuse two complex similarities.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on both OV-AVEL benchmarks, with gains across accuracy and localization metrics.
Also introduces a two-stream variant that substantially improves over the baseline.
papers.selection_reason: Open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization with complex-valued fusion; fits video understanding and video-language tasks.
papers.title: Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization via Complex-Valued Fusion
papers.tldr: A complex-valued fusion network improves open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization by learning how to combine visual-text and audio-text similarities.

papers.abstract: Generating physically plausible videos for solid-gas dynamics is challenging as different phases exhibit distinct dynamics yet remain coupled through physical interactions. We present PAVG, a Phase-Aware Video Generator for solid-gas dynamics and interactions. It employs a dual-branch architecture to explicitly model the distinct dynamics of solids and gases, while spatiotemporal cross-attention captures their physical interactions. This design enables PAVG to preserve phasespecific motion characteristics while producing physically consistent responses across phases. To facilitate this task, we further construct a simulation corpus comprising over 700K physical trajectories across diverse solid, gas, and solid-gas interaction scenarios. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that our PAVG produces videos with improved motion adherence, physical plausibility, and visual quality compared with existing approaches.
authors: Jingfeng Ou, Kun Wang, Rui Zhao, Jingwei Guan, Limin Wang, Chao Dong, Xingyu Zeng
bullets: Addresses the challenge of simulating distinct yet coupled solid and gas behaviors in video.
Uses a dual-branch architecture for phase-specific dynamics and spatiotemporal cross-attention for interactions.
Introduces a simulation corpus with over 700K physical trajectories across solid, gas, and interaction scenarios.
Evaluations show improved motion adherence, physical plausibility, and visual quality over existing approaches.
papers.selection_reason: Physics-grounded video generation of solid-gas dynamics; relevant to video generation and learned environment-dynamics prediction.
papers.title: Phase-aware video generation for physics-grounded dynamics and interactions
papers.tldr: PAVG generates more physically plausible videos of coupled solid–gas dynamics by modeling each phase separately while learning their interactions.

papers.abstract: AI-Native video creation is shifting from isolated video clips toward iterative video creation workflows. However, existing datasets remain largely video clips, representing video generation and editing as separate tasks rather than connected stages of a video creation workflow. In this paper, we introduce Sora100K, a dataset that represents the AI-Native video creation workflow as a structured video creation trajectory. Specifically, we first identify video creation trajectories and decompose them into three subsets according to their structural roles: text-to-video generation records as roots, single-turn video editing records as editing edges, and multi-turn video editing records as complete trajectories. Then, we use a VLM to assign semantic annotations for generation roots and editing-operation annotations for editing edges. A strict construction pipeline further reconstructs source-to-edit lineage, editing order, and intermediate video states while ensuring data quality. Finally, we perform lightweight adaptation on LTX-2 models to assess the supervision value of Sora100K. The results show improvements in visual quality, multi-shot generation, and cross-shot consistency, while successive-turn evaluation reveals that following multi-turn editing instructions remains challenging. Sora100K establishes a new data foundation for AI-Native video creation beyond isolated video clips and toward structured video creation trajectory. The dataset and supplementary materials are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/ysicong/Sora100K.
authors: Sicong Yang, Ruihuan Yang, Jian Lu, Jianfei Yuan, Xiaodong Cun, Xiuli Bi
bullets: Addresses the lack of datasets connecting video generation and iterative editing workflows.
Organizes data into generation roots, single-turn editing edges, and complete multi-turn editing trajectories.
Uses VLM-based semantic and editing-operation annotations plus lineage reconstruction and quality control.
Lightweight adaptation of LTX-2 shows gains in visual quality, multi-shot generation, and cross-shot consistency.
Multi-turn instruction following remains challenging; the dataset is publicly available on Hugging Face.
papers.selection_reason: Dataset and workflow for AI-native video creation and editing; relevant to video generation and diffusion-based video models.
papers.title: From Video Clips to Creation Trajectory: Sora100K for AI-Native Video Creation
papers.tldr: Sora100K reframes AI-native video creation as structured, multi-stage trajectories rather than isolated generation or editing clips.

papers.abstract: Autoregressive video diffusion enables causal video streaming without a bidirectional pass over the full clip, but existing few-step systems usually retain only the opening and most recent frames in a fixed-size KV cache. Once an event leaves this window, later frames can no longer attend to it, a failure we term mid-horizon forgetting. We present Memory Forcing, a few-step streaming method that preserves this missing history without increasing the cache size. Its Archive \& Working Banks partition the cache into sink, archive, and working regions, retaining diverse intermediate events alongside recent motion under fixed memory. Because absolute temporal indices drift outside the training range, Bank-aware RoPE reassigns indices at attention time so each bank remains distinguishable. At 1.3B, Memory Forcing leads on longer clips, shows the smallest drop from 5s to 60s among methods reporting all four lengths, and preserves subjects and scenes through leave-and-return. The same design scales to Wan2.2 5B, producing more physically plausible, realistic, and dynamic videos and, to our knowledge, the first public 5B model on this forcing line.
authors: Jiaming Zhang, Xinyu Wang, Huafeng Shi, Gangshan Wu, Limin Wang
bullets: Existing streaming systems typically retain only initial and recent frames, so intermediate events become inaccessible over long clips.
Archive and Working Banks divide the cache into sink, archive, and working regions to retain both past events and recent motion without increasing memory.
Bank-aware RoPE remaps temporal indices at attention time so the separate memory banks remain distinguishable beyond the training range.
At 1.3B, the method performs strongly on longer clips, with the smallest reported 5s-to-60s degradation among comparable methods.
Scaling to Wan2.2 5B yields more physically plausible, realistic, and dynamic videos, including subject and scene continuity through leave-and-return events.
papers.selection_reason: Streaming video generation with cache partitioning and RoPE addressing; directly relevant to video diffusion, autoregressive video, and KV-cache efficiency.
papers.title: Memory Forcing: Attendable Mid-Horizon History for Streaming Video Generation
papers.tldr: Memory Forcing prevents mid-horizon forgetting in few-step streaming video generation by preserving diverse past events within a fixed-size attention cache.

papers.abstract: Real-time video super-resolution requires high spatio-temporal fidelity under strict latency constraints, challenging diffusion models due to their iterative sampling cost and limited temporal coordination. We propose a streaming-aware framework that adapts pretrained single-image latent diffusion models for efficient video super-resolution (VSR) by exploiting the sequential structure of video streams. Our Cross-Step Attention mechanism reuses intermediate denoising features across adjacent frames and diffusion steps, enabling temporal information exchange without explicit temporal modeling. We further introduce Trajectory-Coupled Diffusion Scheduling, which aligns adjacent diffusion states and provides cleaner intermediate representations for cross-step conditioning, improving temporal coherence.
